title: ACA s. 7 — Arbitration agreement defined (ACA s. 7)

content.overview: Section 7 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 defines an arbitration agreement and prescribes its form. It requires an agreement to submit all or certain disputes arising or to arise between the parties in respect of a defined legal relationship, contractual or otherwise, to arbitration, and requires the agreement to be in writing.

content.study:
Section 7 — Arbitration agreement

Section 7(1) defines an arbitration agreement as an agreement by the parties to submit to arbitration all or certain disputes that have arisen or may arise between them in respect of a defined legal relationship, whether contractual or not.

The definition has identifiable elements:
• an agreement between the parties;
• submission to arbitration;
• all or certain disputes, whether already arisen or prospective;
• disputes connected with a defined legal relationship; and
• the relationship may be contractual or non-contractual.

Section 7(2) recognises two forms: an arbitration clause in a contract or a separate arbitration agreement.

Section 7(3) requires the arbitration agreement to be in writing.

Section 7(4) specifies when the writing requirement is satisfied: a document signed by the parties; an exchange of communications that provides a record of the agreement, including electronic communications; or an exchange of statements of claim and defence in which one party alleges the existence of the agreement and the other does not deny it.

Section 7(5) deals with incorporation by reference. A reference in a written contract to a document containing an arbitration clause constitutes an arbitration agreement where the reference is such as to make that arbitration clause part of the contract.

The statutory inquiry should therefore proceed in sequence: identify the alleged agreement; identify the disputes and defined legal relationship; test whether the agreement submits those disputes to arbitration; test the writing requirement under section 7(3) and (4); and, where incorporation by reference is relied upon, apply section 7(5).

Section 7 is foundational to later provisions that operate on the existence of an arbitration agreement. It should not, however, be collapsed into the separate procedural questions under sections 8, 9 or 11.

sections.heading: 1. Definition and scope
sections.body: Section 7(1) requires an agreement to submit all or certain present or future disputes to arbitration in respect of a defined legal relationship, contractual or otherwise.

sections.heading: 2. Form of arbitration agreement
sections.body: Under section 7(2), an arbitration agreement may be an arbitration clause in a contract or a separate agreement.

sections.heading: 3. Writing requirement
sections.body: Section 7(3) requires the arbitration agreement to be in writing. Section 7(4) identifies statutory situations in which that requirement is satisfied.

sections.heading: 4. Written communications and pleadings
sections.body: Section 7(4) recognises a signed document, qualifying exchanges of letters/telecommunications including electronic communications that provide a record, and an exchange of statements of claim and defence where the agreement is alleged by one party and not denied by the other.

sections.heading: 5. Incorporation by reference
sections.body: Under section 7(5), a reference in a written contract to a document containing an arbitration clause constitutes an arbitration agreement when the reference is such as to make that clause part of the contract.

sections.heading: 6. Application sequence
sections.body: On the record, identify the parties' alleged agreement, its scope, the defined legal relationship, the writing route under section 7(4), and any incorporation by reference under section 7(5). Do not substitute a general assertion of willingness to arbitrate for the statutory requirements.

examples.title: Separate written arbitration agreement
examples.body: Two parties execute a separate written agreement submitting disputes arising from their defined commercial relationship to arbitration. This fits section 7(2) and, if otherwise compliant, the writing requirement in section 7(3).

examples.title: Electronic exchange
examples.body: The parties exchange electronic communications that record their agreement to arbitrate specified disputes. Section 7(4)(b), as amended, expressly includes communication through electronic means where it provides a record of the agreement.

examples.title: Pleadings route
examples.body: In an exchange of statements of claim and defence, one party alleges the existence of an arbitration agreement and the other does not deny it. Section 7(4)(c) treats that situation as an arbitration agreement in writing.

examples.title: Incorporation by reference
examples.body: A written contract refers to another document containing an arbitration clause, and the reference makes that clause part of the contract. Section 7(5) addresses that incorporation route.

hypotheticals.question: A contract contains no arbitration clause, but the parties later sign a separate written arbitration agreement covering specified disputes. Can section 7 recognise it?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, section 7(2) expressly permits an arbitration agreement in the form of a separate agreement, subject to the statutory requirements including writing.

hypotheticals.question: One party alleges an arbitration agreement in its statement of claim and the other party's statement of defence does not deny its existence. What does section 7(4)(c) provide?
hypotheticals.analysis: The exchange falls within the statutory written-form route in section 7(4)(c), provided the statutory factual condition is met: the existence of the agreement is alleged by one party and not denied by the other.

hypotheticals.question: A written contract refers to a document containing an arbitration clause. Is every reference automatically sufficient under section 7(5)?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 7(5) requires the reference to be such as to make the arbitration clause part of the contract. The nature and wording of the reference must therefore be examined.

hypotheticals.question: The parties exchange electronic communications recording an arbitration agreement. Does the statute exclude electronic communications?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 7(4)(b) expressly includes communication through electronic means where the exchange provides a record of the agreement.

misconceptions.trap: An arbitration agreement must always be a standalone document.
misconceptions.correction: Section 7(2) permits an arbitration clause in a contract or a separate arbitration agreement.

misconceptions.trap: Only a physically signed paper can satisfy the writing requirement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 7(4)(b) expressly includes qualifying electronic communications that provide a record of the agreement.

misconceptions.trap: Any reference to another contract automatically incorporates its arbitration clause.
misconceptions.correction: Section 7(5) requires the reference to be such as to make the arbitration clause part of the contract.

misconceptions.trap: Silence in every correspondence proves an arbitration agreement.
misconceptions.correction: The special pleading route in section 7(4)(c) has a precise statutory condition concerning an exchange of statements of claim and defence; it should not be generalised to all silence.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What must be established for an arbitration agreement under section 7?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Establish the agreement to submit all or certain present or future disputes to arbitration, the defined legal relationship, the permissible form, and the writing requirement. If relying on incorporation by reference, separately satisfy section 7(5).
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: The analysis should follow the statutory sequence rather than begin with procedural relief.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should counsel analyse a disputed arbitration agreement?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: First identify the alleged agreement and its scope. Then identify the defined legal relationship and the form relied upon under section 7(2). Next test the writing requirement under section 7(3) and (4), including electronic communications or the pleadings route where applicable. Finally, if incorporation by reference is pleaded, apply section 7(5) to the wording of the written contract and the referenced document.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Keep formation/form questions distinct from later referral, interim-relief or appointment questions.
